To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) firms engage their key supply chain stakeholders to reduce information uncertainty about climate change, (2) the nature of the engagement is influenced by the type of information, and (3) engagement is influenced by firm characteristics.
Firms engage supply chain partners through a range of mechanisms that are consistent with the information processing literature.
Firms engage their key stakeholders to overcome information asymmetries in the supply chain, but the type of engagement varies with the level of information uncertainty and equivocality.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of information processing in managing supply chain climate change risks and the implications this has for the engagement and development of supply chain partners.
how firms manage information asymmetries and equivocality to drive sustainable development.
the role of information in the context of sustainable supply chain management, and how firms engage their supply chain in order to reduce uncertainty and manage climate change information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this paper provides a more detailed understanding on how firms engage supply chains in the context of sustainable supply chain management and climate change.

this paper contributes to literatures on supply chain management, information management and climate change management by developing a framework that explains how firms engage their supply chains in the context of carbon disclosure and climate change.

firms engage their supply chains in a variety of different ways in order to obtain, process and transfer information related to climate change, but that this engagement is primarily focused on the reduction of uncertainty around indirect emissions.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have provided an empirical study of the engagement of supply chain actors in climate change information processing, with a focus on how this engagement relates to the information processing theory.
firms use a variety of engagement approaches to manage climate change related information asymmetry and equivocality.
we have provided evidence of how firms engage with their supply chain partners to manage information in the context of sustainable supply chain management and climate change.
The main takeaway from our work is that
firms are actively seeking to manage information asymmetry and equivocality in their supply chains through engagement with key stakeholders.
firms are increasingly engaging with their supply chain partners to manage the information asymmetry and equivocality around climate change related issues.
firms are not just seeking information on indirect GHG emissions, they are seeking to understand and manage a wide range of information about climate change risks and opportunities.
